title: Gold fact: add `supply_mix` + `t` to fact_supply_share and migrate the global-only consumers
description: Union both silver supply tables into fact_supply_share with a supply_mix discriminator ('global' | 'eu_sourcing') and carry `t` through, per spec § Data Architecture → Gold Layer item 2. Then migrate every existing consumer that assumed the fact was global-only.
acceptanceCriteria: fact_supply_share grain is material × stage × country × year × supply_mix, with `supply_mix` and `t` present as spec'd.
Rows are unioned from silver_globalsupplyshares and silver_eusupplyshares with supply_mix stamped at read time; the two mixes are never summed together.
MIGRATION — v_supply_concentration_risk filters supply_mix = 'global', preserving its pre-DEC-001 meaning. Without this it silently double-counts once EU rows land.
The existing quality-scoring, unmapped-audit (gold_unmapped_supply_audit) and both v_fact_supply_share_* views work correctly across both mixes.
A row-count check confirms global-mix row counts are unchanged from before this task — the EU rows are additive, not a re-partition of existing data.

METHODOLOGY DECISION RESOLVED 2026-07-30 (Erik, inline) — HOW `t` COMBINES IN THE TERRITORY ROLLUP. The rollup at silver-to-gold2 (~line 1999) groups by (material_key, stage_key, country_key, year) and SUMs share_pct, because territory aliases map several source countries onto one dim country (live case: Antimony/P China 51.8% t=1.1 export-restricted + Hong Kong 0.3% t=1.0 baseline -> China 52.1%). An in-code note left by task-024/028 flagged that carrying `t` through would require defining how it combines, and called it a methodology decision for DEC-001, not an implementation detail. DEC-001 fixes the formula HHI_WGI,t = sum_c (S^c)^2 * WGI^c * t^c but is silent on rollup aggregation. CHOSEN: SHARE-WEIGHTED MEAN — t_merged = sum(share_i * t_i) / sum(share_i). For the live case: (51.8*1.1 + 0.3*1.0)/52.1 = 1.0994. RATIONALE: it is the only rule that preserves the trade-weighted supply quantity sum(S*t) exactly across the rollup (57.28 before and after); t is a per-flow multiplier in the DEC-001 formula, so a merged flow's effective t is the share-weighted average of its constituents. It is also an exact no-op on the ~2560 non-colliding grains, matching the behaviour of the existing SUM/MIN/MAX aggregations. Rejected: MAX (overstates, 57.31), dominant-constituent (discards the minor row, unstable at near-equal shares), MIN (understates by 9% — MIN suits data_quality_score because that is a trust score; t is a risk multiplier).

FILES_AFFECTED WIDENED 2026-07-30: adding supply_mix changes the fact grain, so fabric/data_quality_checks.Notebook/notebook-content.py must change too — grain_checks at line 1571-1577 declares fact_supply_share's key list as [material_key, stage_key, country_key, year]. Left unchanged, grain_uniqueness will flag every EU row as a duplicate grain the moment the union lands and fail the pipeline at 0% tolerance. DESIGN: the two silver tables are unioned at READ time (strict unionByName, no allowMissingColumns) with supply_mix stamped per source, BEFORE any cleaning. Consequence: the '<1%' -> 0.5 convention, the dim joins, quality scoring and the territory rollup are each expressed exactly once and apply identically to both mixes — task-028's single-source-of-truth rule survives and there is no per-source special-casing. `t` is cast string->double at that point with a counter that warns if any non-numeric value casts to NULL (observability, not suppression — Fabric runs ANSI off so it would otherwise be silent).

GRAIN: supply_mix joins the rollup groupBy AND the _dup_grain assert AND data_quality_checks' grain_checks key list (all three must stay in step). The t rollup implements the share-weighted mean decided 2026-07-30, with NULL rows excluded from both numerator and denominator (a missing t cannot bias the mean down), a zero-denominator fallback to the unweighted mean, and all-NULL yielding NULL rather than inventing a value.

MIGRATION RULE (criterion 3 + 4) — the dividing line is AGGREGATION. A consumer that only filters/decorates rows cannot double-count, so it stays mix-inclusive and exposes supply_mix for the caller to pivot on; a consumer that aggregates over the fact would blend the two mixes and silently change its own pre-DEC-001 meaning, so it is pinned to global. Applied: v_fact_supply_share_high_confidence MIX-INCLUSIVE; v_fact_supply_share_complete MIX-INCLUSIVE; v_supply_concentration_risk GLOBAL-ONLY (WHERE supply_mix='global' — criterion 3); quality_by_material now groups BY supply_mix; gold_unmapped_supply_audit gains a supply_mix column; gold_country_coverage_matrix's has_supply left GLOBAL-ONLY (its published meaning is 'appears as a worldwide producer'); gold_low_confidence_audit left GLOBAL-ONLY (no mix discriminator in its contract — unioning EU would inflate `frequency` on existing rows rather than add new ones; widening it needs a supply_mix column first — FOLLOW-UP).

SIDE EFFECT HANDLED: gold_dim_material now also gathers materials from silver_eusupplyshares. Without it, any EU-only material would find no dim row, land on the 'Unknown Material' placeholder and be reported as an unmapped-material quality failure — a false signal manufactured by the union. Additive only; the dim is keyed on the standardised name.

FIX A — consumer left double-counting. data_quality_analysis.Notebook :160-170 computed SUM(share_pct) grouped only by quality_category, blending both mixes (total would read ~200 for a material whose global and EU shares each sum to ~100). It is the identical construct already migrated as quality_by_material. Now groups BY supply_mix. files_affected widened a second time to include this notebook — the verifier filed a template_gap marker noting the consumer sweep is being done reactively per-file rather than enumerated at decomposition time.

FIX B — the criterion-5 assert was a tautology. It computed _expected_global_rows from fact_supply_share_final itself and then compared that frame against it, so both sides moved in lockstep; the verifier proved it could not fail over 200 randomized frames. Replaced with an EXTERNAL baseline: the fact table as it exists in the lakehouse BEFORE write_tbl overwrites it (pre-task shape with no supply_mix column -> its total row count IS the old global-only count; already-migrated -> its 'global' slice; absent -> reported as no-baseline first run). Deliberately downgraded from assert to a reported PASS/DIVERGENCE, because criterion 5 is a one-time migration check while a hard assert would fail every future legitimate annual source refresh — the message distinguishes the two cases explicitly.

TEST-PROTOCOL DEFECT FOUND BY ERIK 2026-07-30: verify-agent's protocol put the v_supply_concentration_risk baseline query in the SQL analytics endpoint, where it fails with 'Invalid object name'. The three v_* objects are created via spark.sql('CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ...') in silver-to-gold2, so they are SPARK CATALOG views; the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint exposes Delta tables only and cannot see them. Any check touching v_supply_concentration_risk, v_fact_supply_share_complete or v_fact_supply_share_high_confidence must run in a NOTEBOOK, not the SQL endpoint. Consequence worth tracking beyond this task: these views are invisible to the SQL endpoint and to DirectLake (which reads Delta tables), so they are notebook-only artifacts — anything in the semantic model or Power BI cannot consume them.

CRITERION-3 BASELINE (partial) CAPTURED 2026-07-30 pre-pipeline-run, via NOTEBOOK (Spark view, invisible to the SQL endpoint). Top-10 by max_country_share: Europium, Ytterbium, Holmium, Lutetium, Gadolinium, Erbium, Yttrium, Dysprosium, Terbium, Thulium — ALL stage=Processing, max_country_share=100.0, supplier_country_count=1, concentration_risk_level=Critical. Confirms the pre-task view means 'worldwide production concentration' and that the heavy rare earths are single-source at processing.

⚠️ TOP-10 IS NOT A VALID BEFORE/AFTER DIFF for criterion 3: every row ties at max_country_share=100.0 and the ORDER BY carries no tiebreaker, so the post-run query can legitimately return a different arbitrary 10 through non-deterministic ordering — indistinguishable from real corruption. Replaced with an order-independent whole-view fingerprint (GROUP BY concentration_risk_level with COUNT, SUM/AVG of max_country_share, SUM of supplier_country_count, plus total row count). Any EU rows leaking past the supply_mix='global' filter move those aggregates. General lesson for future test protocols: never diff a LIMIT/TOP-N sample when the sort key has ties.

⚠️ GOTCHA THAT COST A DIAGNOSTIC DETOUR — the SQL analytics endpoint returned 'Invalid column name supply_mix / t' for HOURS after the write succeeded. The endpoint is a separate T-SQL engine over a CACHED copy of the lakehouse schema and lags badly on SCHEMA CHANGES to a table it has already cached (observed ~7h stale, not the 'minute or two' assumed). Spark read the correct schema immediately. Rule: after any column addition, verify in a NOTEBOOK, not the SQL endpoint — an 'Invalid column name' there is not evidence the write failed. Diagnosed by pulling the pipeline job instances and the live notebook definition via the Fabric REST API rather than trusting either surface.
